system.name: BlitzScale
system.one_liner: a fast, live autoscaling system for large-model serving that uses O(1) host caching

content.key_idea: BlitzScale models cluster networking at two levels: a leaf-to-spine RDMA topology for scale-out traffic between nodes, and a full-mesh NVLink group for scale-up traffic between the GPUs inside one node/cluster.
content.reading_order: From the Spine network cloud down to leaf switches and their nodes on the left, then to the GPU cluster box and its exploded NIC/GPU/NVLink mesh on the right.

summary: Figure 10 shows how BlitzScale abstracts a GPU cluster's network into two layers for its scaling model. On the left, a Spine network cloud connects down to leaf switches (L1, L2, ...), each linking over a scale-out RDMA network to a set of server nodes (Node1...NodeM under L1, NodeM+1... under L2); GPUs behind the same leaf switch are treated as fully meshed at min(BWi, BWj) bandwidth. On the right, the 'A GPU cluster' box is exploded to show what fast scale-up networking looks like inside one group: each GPU's NIC carries its own BWi bandwidth, and the GPUs themselves are joined by a full-mesh ScaleUp Network such as NVLink, whose 1,600-3,600 Gbps interconnect makes scaling within the group essentially free. The spine network itself is deliberately left unmodelled, relying on existing multipathing protocols.
